one_line_contribution: A measurement study that asks how much of a procedural experience-memory bank's benchmark gain survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) has been given the same training episodes, operationalized as a substitution ratio S, plus the stronger engineering claim that the whole bank can be compiled once, offline, into a frozen instruction and per-instance retrieval deleted with no loss.
closest_prior_work: Three lines threaten it, none of which the proposal cites. (a) ACE / Agentic Context Engineering (arXiv 2510.04618) treats an accumulating natural-language playbook as the container for training-episode experience and benchmarks it directly against GEPA on agent tasks, which contradicts the proposal's claim that 'no published work uses one as the control for the other'. (b) Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv 2504.07952) and Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429, offline variant) already build a single static distilled text artifact from past episodes and inject it with no per-instance retrieval, which is exactly arm C; AWM's offline-vs-online comparison is a weak-form version of prediction 3 and it already reports offline induction is competitive. (c) ExpeL itself (2308.10144) ablates its global insight list against its retrieved trajectory pool, so 'do the retrieved per-instance items add anything over the globally injected distillate?' is partly an existing ExpeL ablation. What survives as new is the specific accounting object (substitution ratio at matched training episodes and matched injected tokens) and the non-compilable positive control, which is a real but modest contribution.
strongest_objection: S is not diagnostic of the mechanism the paper names. On a bounded accuracy scale, any intervention that raises the no-memory baseline by a large amount will shrink a second intervention's marginal gain through simple saturation and sub-additivity in accuracy space, whether or not the two containers hold the same information. The design has no arm that separates 'I1 already contains memory's information' from 'memory's gain shrinks on top of any stronger baseline'. I3 controls prompt length, not baseline strength, and the primary endpoint is computed on the raw accuracy scale even though the CIs come from a logistic model, so an effect that is perfectly additive in logits will be reported as S near 0.5-0.7 and written up as substitution. Second, the design fails on its own arithmetic: with the stated SE of 2.0 points on the numerator and roughly 1.4-2.0 on a denominator gated at 10 points, the delta-method SE on S is about 0.2, so a 95 percent bootstrap CI has half-width near 0.4; prediction 1 requires a point estimate of 0.6 whose CI excludes 0.3, which is unattainable at n=600 with 3 optimizer seeds unless the true S is 0.75 or higher. The proposal's own 'cannot resolve S better than roughly plus/minus 0.2' is a one-SE number being read as a confidence interval.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add an information-mismatched but strength-matched instruction arm: GEPA run on a disjoint task pool (or on the same episodes with a scrambled reward signal), padded to the same length and selected to deliver a comparable I1-vs-I0 gain. If memory's gain collapses on top of that instruction too, S measures saturation, not substitution; if it survives, the informational reading is earned. An accuracy-matched non-prompt strengthener (self-consistency, larger step budget) is an acceptable second form of the same control. (2) Demote S to a descriptive secondary and make the primary endpoint the memory-by-instruction interaction term on the logit scale from the mixed-effects model already specified, which is the quantity that is actually additive. (3) Fix the fairness constraint in the protocol, not just the prose: the bank uses 500 E1 episodes while GEPA gets 300 rollouts, and the precheck permits enriching the bank with more training episodes until it clears 10 points without re-running GEPA on the enlarged split. As written this both violates 'exactly the same training episodes' and tunes the denominator of S upward on a dev split, which biases S toward the hypothesis. Freeze the bank before any gate readout, or pre-register the enrichment rule, re-run the optimizer on the final split, and report S for every bank built. (4) Convert predictions 2, 3 and 7 to formal equivalence tests (TOST) with margins above the MDE; as stated, 'within 2 points' on a design with a 4-point MDE is confirmed by failure to reject, which is the exact trap the Measurement section elsewhere avoids. (5) Re-power the positive control: predicting that I0xM2dup loses to I0xM1dup by at least 5 points on an n=300 subset whose stated MDE is about 6 points means the load-bearing instrument can fail to fire for power reasons, which destroys the 'a null is a finding' argument. Either seed B-dup to produce a much larger effect and say so, or run it at full n. (6) Resolve TERMS-Bench and cite ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet and Agent Workflow Memory.
missing_baseline: An instruction arm that is optimized but informationally disjoint from the memory bank: GEPA run on a held-out or unrelated task pool, or on the same episodes with a shuffled/scrambled metric, length-matched to I1 and chosen to produce a similar I1-vs-I0 accuracy gain. Without it, cell 6 (I1xM1) cannot distinguish container substitution from diminishing returns, and every headline number is compatible with both. A secondary omission: no faithful ExpeL configuration is run. M1 is described as top-k=7 retrieval over distilled insights plus condensed trajectories, whereas ExpeL injects its insight list globally and retrieves only trajectories; that difference means arm C (compiled static) is being compared against a variant of ExpeL rather than ExpeL, and a reviewer will ask whether the compiled-vs-retrieved result is an artifact of how M1 was assembled.
preprint_collision: Diligent in form, unreliable in substance, and with a specific known miss. The check does the right structural thing by retracting five previously cited works (ActMem, MAS-PromptBench, TERMS-Bench, MemAPO, 2602.11243) that the current search could not return, but that retraction is itself the problem: it establishes that the search tooling produced fabricated or unstable hits in at least one direction, which means the surviving citations (MemDelta 2606.29914, EvoClinician 2601.22964, 2603.02473, 2605.21768, 2603.18272) carry no more warrant than the retracted ones. The single most threatening item is then left unresolved by a conditional ('if that work exists as described'), when TERMS-Bench is precisely the structural precedent for the paper's core logical move. The check also states that no OpenReview 2026 sweep was performed, and it misses three verifiable 2024-2025 preprints that bear directly on the risky prediction: ACE (2510.04618), which already runs a GEPA-vs-accumulated-context comparison and therefore falsifies the Related Work sentence that no one has used one as a control for the other; Dynamic Cheatsheet (2504.07952); and Agent Workflow Memory (2409.07429), whose offline variant is arm C under a different name. Given that these are exactly the neighborhood the check was supposed to sweep, I treat the novelty of the compiled-static instrument as unestablished rather than merely uncertain.
